gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 directly identifies the failed universal standard-form representation claim: a general vertically closed form can contain arbitrary prolongation-coordinate differentials rather than only the displayed nearest-neighbour mixed shifts. Its proposed repair specifically restricts the scope or proves the representation only under the needed first-order structure.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify that the claimed universal nearest-neighbour representation of vertically closed multisymplectic forms is not established and is false for general prolongation-coordinate forms.

component_coverage.gold_component: The universal assertion that every admissible vertically closed form has the displayed nearest-neighbour representation is false because general forms may involve arbitrary prolongation-coordinate differentials.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly contrasts the asserted standard representation with general terms indexed by arbitrary multi-indices and proposes either proving the restricted form from first-order structure or restricting the scope, which directly diagnoses the gold defect.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 questions whether a specific first-order Lagrangian form follows for general multisymplectic systems, but it does not recognize the gold defect that the construction proves only inclusion of original solutions in the Euler–Lagrange solution set and not the reverse implication required for equivalence.

ISSUE-004 also challenges a domain claim, but concerns existence of a Hamiltonian on a full prolongation space due to failure of vertical closedness. It does not identify the logarithm and reciprocal as imposing positivity of the second component or the mismatch with the declared real fibre.
